katex.intro: Mathematical formulas are written in LaTeX and rendered by KaTeX, in any text or exercise block. Every example below is editable: use it as a starting point.

delimiters.title: Delimiters
delimiters.body: An inline formula goes between $…$, a centered one between $$…$$. A few rules keep prices from turning into formulas:
delimiters.ruleNoSpace: no space right after the opening $ nor right before the closing $;
delimiters.ruleDigit: a closing $ followed by a digit stays plain text (“10$ and 20$”);
delimiters.ruleBlockLine: a $$…$$ block must close at the end of a line (multi-line content allowed);

basics.title: Fractions, powers, roots
basics.body: \frac{a}{b} for a fraction (\dfrac forces display size inline), ^ for exponents, _ for subscripts — braces required beyond one character —, \sqrt{x} and \sqrt[n]{x} for roots.

operators.title: Sums, integrals, limits
operators.body: Big operators take their bounds as sub/superscripts: \sum, \int, \lim, \prod. \, inserts a thin space (before dx for instance).

symbols.title: Greek letters and symbols
symbols.body: Greek letters are \alpha, \pi, \Omega…; comparisons \le \ge \ne \approx; operations \times \cdot \pm; sets \mathbb{R}, \in, \subset, \cup, \cap; arrows \rightarrow, \implies, \iff.

matrices.title: Matrices
matrices.body: pmatrix (parentheses), bmatrix (brackets) and vmatrix (determinant) environments: & separates columns, \\ separates rows.

systems.title: Systems and alignment
systems.body: cases for piecewise definitions, aligned to line up several equalities on the = sign (marked with &).

text.title: Text inside a formula
text.body: \text{…} inserts upright text inside a formula; \, \quad and \qquad control spacing.

errors.title: Invalid formulas
errors.body: An invalid formula never breaks the block: it renders in red with its source visible until you fix it.

mhchem.intro: Chemical notation is written inside a KaTeX formula, between dollar signs, with the \ce{…} command (mhchem extension); \pu{…} writes a physical quantity with its unit. Subscripts and charges are placed automatically. Every example is editable.

first.title: First equation
first.body: Inside \ce{…}, formulas are written as they are read: digits after a symbol become subscripts, the coefficient goes before the species, -> draws the reaction arrow.

species.title: Ions, states and nuclei
species.body: The charge follows ^ (Cu^2+, SO4^2-); the physical state goes in parentheses: (s), (l), (g), (aq). A dot joins the parts of a hydrate; ^{A}_{Z} gives the mass number and atomic number of a nucleus.

arrows.title: Arrows and equilibria
arrows.body: -> reaction, <- reverse direction, <=> equilibrium, <-> resonance. Text above the arrow goes in square brackets: ->[{catalyst}]. A lone v marks a precipitate, a lone ^ a gas release.

units.title: Quantities and units
units.body: \pu{…} writes a value and its unit with correct spacing: e for the power of ten (1.6e-19), a dot or * to multiply units (m.s^-2), / to divide (kJ/mol).

errors.title: Always between dollar signs
errors.body: \ce and \pu are KaTeX commands: outside a $…$ or $$…$$ formula, they stay plain text. Invalid notation is shown in red, like any invalid formula.

mermaid.intro: A “mermaid” code block describes a diagram as text; it renders automatically (the source stays visible until rendering runs). The first two examples are editable.

flowchart.title: Flowchart
flowchart.body: graph TD (top-down) or graph LR (left-right). Nodes: [rectangle], {decision diamond}, (rounded). Arrows --> take a label between pipes: -->|yes|.

sequence.title: Sequence diagram
sequence.body: sequenceDiagram describes exchanges: participant declares an actor (with an alias), ->> a solid arrow, -->> a dashed reply.

gallery.title: Other diagram types
gallery.body: Mermaid covers many more needs — each source below can be copied into a mermaid block:

theme.title: Theme
theme.body: Diagrams automatically follow the app's light/dark mode — nothing to configure; do not hardcode colors in the source.

math.title: Limitation: no LaTeX inside nodes
math.body: $…$ formulas are not rendered inside a mermaid node (a note under the diagram reminds you). Write the formula in the text around the diagram.

errors.title: Invalid diagrams
errors.body: An invalid source does not break the rest of the block: the source is kept with the error message as a caption.

geogebra.intro: A “geogebra” code block embeds a GeoGebra activity published on geogebra.org, displayed in an interactive frame.

findId.title: Finding an activity's identifier
findId.body: Open the activity on geogebra.org: the identifier is the code at the end of the address. That code alone is what you provide — never the full address.

keys.title: Block keys
keys.body: One key per line, in key=value format:
keys.id: material identifier (required, letters and digits only);
keys.height: height in pixels (default 450, bounds 150–900). Non-numeric value → default, out of bounds → clamped.

invalid.title: Invalid identifier
invalid.body: An identifier that is not strictly alphanumeric (a URL, for instance) never renders a frame: a notice points it out.

print.title: Printing and PDF export
print.body: A GeoGebra activity is interactive and cannot be printed: in the PDF export it is replaced by the note “Interactive content: see the online version”.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.body: Content is loaded from geogebra.org (external, sandboxed frame): students viewing the course load a third-party resource. Worth factoring into your school's data policy.

jsxgraph.intro: A “jsxgraph” code block draws a mathematical figure (curves, points) rendered locally — no external service —, interactive (pan, zoom) and printable.

first.title: First plot
first.body: equation= plots the curve of a function of x. Edit the equation below and watch the plot.

syntax.title: Equation syntax
syntax.functions: usual functions: sin, cos, tan, exp, log, sqrt, abs.

multiple.title: Several curves and points
multiple.body: Repeat equation= to overlay curves, and point=x,y to mark points (here the intersections).

bbox.title: Framing
bbox.body: bbox=xmin,ymax,xmax,ymin sets the visible area (default -5,5,5,-5). Mind the order: top-left corner then bottom-right corner.

errors.title: Invalid input
errors.body: A malformed line is ignored (the figure draws what is valid); an unparsable equation shows a notice instead of the figure.

print.title: Printing and PDF export
print.body: The figure is drawn as SVG: it goes into the course PDF export as-is.

tikz.intro: A “tikz” code block compiles LaTeX/TikZ code into an SVG directly in the browser — no external service —, crisp vector rendering and natively printable.

first.title: First drawing
first.body: The block's content is the body of a tikzpicture environment (added automatically if missing). Edit the drawing below.

advanced.title: TikZ options
advanced.body: The usual tikzpicture options (scale, fill colors…) are available by writing out the environment with its brackets.

print.title: Printing and PDF export
print.body: The rendering is a vector SVG: it goes into the course PDF export as-is, with crisp text and lines.

timeline.intro: A “timeline” code block draws a timeline: periods as bands below the axis, events above it. The timeline follows the light or dark theme and prints as is. Every example is editable.

first.title: First timeline
first.body: period=start,end,label draws a period; repeat the line to add more. The axis bounds and ticks are computed automatically.

events.title: Events and precise dates
events.dates: a date is written YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD (1789-07-14);
events.labels: the label is everything after the comma: it may contain commas itself;
events.lanes: items that are too close are stacked on several rows instead of overlapping.

bounds.title: Bounds and ticks
bounds.body: start= and end= set the axis bounds (anything beyond is clipped), step= the tick interval in years. A step too fine for the timeline's width is replaced by a round one.

bce.title: Before Christ
bce.body: A negative year is BC: -52 is shown as “52 BC”. The axis is continuous: it ignores the missing year 0 of the historical calendar, a one-year gap that does not matter at the scale of a timeline.

errors.title: Invalid lines
errors.body: A malformed line (unreadable date, missing label or period end) is ignored: the timeline draws what is valid and reports how many lines were ignored.

print.title: Printing and PDF export
print.body: The timeline is drawn as SVG: it goes as is into the course PDF export, in light colors.

smiles.intro: A “smiles” code block draws the skeletal formula of one or more molecules, each described on one line in SMILES notation. The drawing is computed in the browser, with no external service, on a light board in both themes. Every example is editable.

first.title: First molecule
first.body: One line = one molecule. The optional caption follows a vertical bar |; without it, the molecule is shown alone.

syntax.title: Writing SMILES
syntax.body: SMILES notation describes the molecule atom by atom:
syntax.atoms: atoms are written with their symbol (C, O, N, Cl…); hydrogens are implicit;
syntax.bonds: = marks a double bond, # a triple bond;
syntax.branches: a branch goes in parentheses: CC(C)O is propan-2-ol.

rings.title: Rings and aromatics
rings.body: A digit opens then closes a ring (C1CCCCC1); lowercase atoms are aromatic (c1ccccc1, benzene).

ions.title: Ions and separate species
ions.body: Square brackets for a charged atom or explicit hydrogens: [NH4+], [O-]. A dot separates unbonded species: [Na+].[Cl-].

errors.title: Invalid SMILES
errors.body: An unreadable SMILES shows a notice instead of its molecule; the other lines of the block are drawn normally.

print.title: Printing and PDF export
print.body: Molecules are drawn as SVG: they go as is into the course PDF export.

vegalite.intro: A “vegalite” code block draws a data chart described in JSON with the Vega-Lite grammar: the values, the kind of mark and what each axis stands for. The chart is computed in the browser and drawn on a light board. Every example is editable.

first.title: First chart
first.body: A specification brings together three parts:
first.data: data.values: the data, one object per table row;
first.mark: mark: the kind of mark — bar, line, point, area, arc (pie)…;
first.encoding: encoding: which column goes to which channel (x, y, color, theta…) and its type (quantitative, nominal, ordinal, temporal).

measures.title: Measurements and regression
measures.body: Layers stack several marks on the same axes: here the measured points and their regression line, computed by the regression transform.

layers.title: Two scales on one chart
layers.body: With resolve, each layer keeps its own vertical axis: this is how a climate chart works, precipitation as bars and temperature as a line.

errors.title: Inline data only
errors.body: Data is written inside the specification (data.values): loading from a URL is refused, so that no chart makes a request to a third-party site from students' browsers. Invalid JSON or an invalid specification likewise shows a notice with the error message.

print.title: Printing and PDF export
print.body: The chart is drawn as static SVG: it goes as is into the course PDF export. Tooltips and interactive selections are not supported.

abc.intro: An “abc” code block engraves sheet music written in ABC notation, a text format where each note is a letter. The tune plays on the piano in one click, with no external service, and prints. Every example is editable.

first.title: First tune
first.body: A few headers, one per line, then the notes:
first.headerX: X: the tune number (1 is enough) and T: its title;
first.headerMeter: M: the time signature (4/4, 3/4…), L: the default note length (1/4 = a quarter note), Q: the tempo;
first.headerKey: K: the key (C, G, F, Dm…) — always the last header, right before the notes.

notes.title: Pitches and durations
notes.body: One letter per note, a vertical bar between measures:
notes.pitch: C D E F G A B for the middle octave, c d e… for the octave above; a comma lowers by an octave (C,), an apostrophe raises (c');
notes.duration: a digit multiplies the default length (C2, C4), a slash divides it (C/2 or C/); z is a rest;
notes.accidentals: ^ sharp, _ flat, = natural, before the note (^F, _B); the key signature is applied automatically.

chords.title: Chords and rhythms
chords.body: A chord symbol in double quotes ("D", "Am") shows above the staff and accompanies the tune on playback. F>E writes a dotted rhythm (dotted F followed by a sixteenth-note E).

audio.title: Playback
audio.body: The Listen button plays the tune on the piano; notes load on first playback, and only one tune plays at a time. Only the piano is available: %%MIDI instrument directives are ignored.
audio.credit: Piano sounds: Frank Wen's Fluid R3 GM soundfont, under the Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 license, sampled by the midi-js-soundfonts project.

errors.title: Incomplete sheet music
errors.body: With no notes at all, the block shows a notice. A line the ABC parser does not understand is reported in collapsed warnings under the sheet music, which stays visible.

print.title: Printing and PDF export
print.body: Sheet music is engraved as SVG: it goes as is into the course PDF export, without the Listen button.

sql.intro: An “sql” code block becomes a runnable query: students run it, edit it and run it again, and results show as a table. The SQLite engine runs in their browser, with no account or server, and is only downloaded on the first click on Run. Every example is editable.

first.title: First query
first.body: Click Run in the preview: the query runs and the result shows under the code. Edit lets you change it, Reset goes back to the course code.

setup.title: Setting up a database
setup.body: Everything before the -- @query line sets up the database (creating and filling tables): this part is collapsed for students. What follows is the query they see and edit. The marker is an SQL comment: the block stays valid SQL.

queries.title: Joins and aggregates
queries.body: All of SQLite's SQL is available: joins, GROUP BY, subqueries, window functions… Each SELECT in the query produces its own table.

limits.title: Good to know
limits.independent: each run starts from a fresh database: a course's blocks are independent, and a change (INSERT, UPDATE) does not survive the next run;
limits.timeout: a query running longer than 5 seconds (endless recursion, huge cartesian product) is interrupted;
limits.rows: a result shows at most 200 rows, and the total count is given;
limits.engine: the engine (about 0.7 MB) is downloaded only once, on the first click, then cached by the browser.

errors.title: Errors
errors.body: An SQL error shows SQLite's message under the code, saying whether it comes from the setup or the query. Run the example below to see it.

print.title: Printing and PDF export
print.body: The code and the last displayed result go into the PDF export; buttons are hidden.
